beats.setting: The Meryton assembly rooms at the height of the evening: chandeliers lit, fiddlers in the gallery, long lines of country dancers down the floor, the neighbourhood packed along the walls.

beats.text: The Meryton rooms are full to the walls and bright as day. Mr Bingley was to have come tonight and has not, and every eye in the room has gone instead to the friend who came without him: tall, handsome, worth ten thousand a year, standing by the far wall and pleased with nothing. Sir William Lucas has seen you come in. He is already on his way.

beats.speaker: Sir William Lucas
beats.direction: Sir William crosses the floor with the air of a man delivering good news to the world at large.
beats.line: "Miss Frost, allow me, Sir William Lucas, and I shall introduce you to everyone of consequence!"

beats.speaker: Sir William Lucas
beats.line: "Even Mr. Darcy, who has danced at St. James's itself, shall not escape the floor tonight!"

options.text: Sir William, does St. James's teach a man to refuse a partner?
A man who condescends to dance still condescends, Sir William.
I find I prefer to watch Mr. Darcy appraise the room first.
She turns her gaze toward the far wall where Darcy stands.

beats.text: Sir William, does St. James's teach a man to refuse a partner?

beats.speaker: Sir William Lucas
beats.direction: Sir William drops his chin and leans in, one hand raised to shield the confidence.
beats.line: "Between ourselves, Miss Frost, I mean to put you before Mr. Darcy before supper is served."

beats.text: Across the room, that knot of fan-wielding young ladies watches Mr. Darcy as if he were a comet; he looks nowhere.
Mr Darcy is wanted by the whole room and wants none of it.

options.text: Tell me, Sir William, does St. James's improve a man's manners or merely his posture?
I will not be placed before Mr. Darcy like a dish at supper.
He looks at nothing, and yet everyone looks at him.
She turns the fan slowly in her hand and says nothing.

beats.text: Tell me, Sir William, does St. James's improve a man's manners or merely his posture?

beats.speaker: Sir William Lucas
beats.direction: Sir William presses one hand to his breast, closes his eyes, and bows low and slow, as though the fiddlers are trumpets and the assembly room is St James's itself.

beats.title: Charlotte's bet: nobody will make Mr Darcy dance

beats.text: Nobody will make Mr Darcy dance tonight. That is Charlotte's wager, and she has taken it.

options.text: Sir William, then lead me to him, I have a bet to collect.
I will not be placed before him like a dish at supper.
She sets her glass down and crosses the floor toward Mr Darcy.
A man who looks nowhere is looking at everything.

beats.text: Sir William, then lead me to him, I have a bet to collect.
Sir William leads you down the room as though to the King, and presents you to Mr Darcy, loud enough for half the floor, as the wittiest young lady in Hertfordshire.

beats.setting: A quiet stretch of floor by the wall, the loud room at their backs, the next set not yet called.

beats.text: Mr Darcy has not yet spoken; he simply looks at her, measuring.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He holds her gaze a moment longer than courtesy strictly requires, then inclines his head a precise degree.
beats.line: "Hertfordshire sets a modest ceiling, Miss Frost. I wonder if you find it so."

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.line: "Sir William's superlatives seldom disappoint. In your case, they have not misled him."

options.text: Then Sir William and I are, for once, in perfect agreement.
Hertfordshire's ceiling, Mr Darcy, is rather your floor.
I glance past him toward the empty set forming without us.
She holds his gaze and says nothing, one brow barely raised.

beats.text: Hertfordshire's ceiling, Mr Darcy, is rather your floor.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.line: "Then I trust you find it comfortable, Miss Frost. Most do."

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He turns his gaze to the middle distance, as though the matter is already concluded.

options.text: I find it remarkably so, do you not, Mr Darcy?
You conclude the matter rather before I have finished, sir.
You insist nothing here is worth your attention, yet here you look.
She turns her face toward the dancers, unhurried.

beats.text: You insist nothing here is worth your attention, yet here you look.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He turns back to her, precisely as described. His gaze settles on her and does not move.
beats.line: "I assure you, I look at nothing in particular."

options.text: Nothing in particular, and yet so very particularly at me.
That is precisely the look a man gives a thing he means to dismiss.
I find the chandelier equally riveting, Mr Darcy, shall we compare notes.
She turns her face toward the dancers and says nothing at all.

beats.text: I find the chandelier equally riveting, Mr Darcy, shall we compare notes.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: A short, involuntary sound escapes him; his jaw tightens immediately after.
beats.line: "You have the advantage of me, Miss Frost."

beats.text: The laugh breaks free, brief, unguarded, and Mr Darcy goes quite still, as if surprised by his own treason.

options.text: Only in this room, Mr Darcy; elsewhere I suspect you lead.
An advantage implies you were not already looking down.
I confess I am still learning which corners here are safe.
She turns her face toward the dancers and is still.

beats.text: I confess I am still learning which corners here are safe.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: Something in his posture shifts, almost imperceptibly, at the word safe.
beats.line: "My sister is sixteen. She would sooner face a regiment than a room like this one."

beats.text: There is someone he is gentle with, and he has just shown her.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.line: "I was not so different, once, and have perhaps not changed as much as I suppose."

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He looks away, toward the middle of the room, as if the admission had not been made at all.

options.text: Then perhaps the room is not entirely beneath you after all.
Looking away does not unsay it, Mr Darcy.
That corner of young ladies has watched you all evening, I think.
She holds perfectly still, watching him decide where to look.

beats.text: That corner of young ladies has watched you all evening, I think.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He glances, just once, toward the corner, then looks away.
beats.line: "I did not come here to be looked at."

beats.text: Charlotte, across the room, lowers her fan and taps it once against her palm, the wager, silently renewed.

options.text: Yet here you stand, Mr Darcy, remarkably visible for a man unwilling.
I did not come to be looked at either, and yet.
Honestly, even the chandelier seems to be performing tonight.
She lets the silence sit, her eyes level, her expression entirely composed.

beats.text: Honestly, even the chandelier seems to be performing tonight.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: The corner of his mouth moves, just once.
beats.line: "Sir William is waving at us. He believes he has accomplished something."

beats.text: Sir William's wave grows more emphatic, his satisfaction visible from thirty feet.
The set is called; couples stir; Mr Darcy's gaze moves once to the forming line, then back to her.

options.text: Sir William always believes he has accomplished something, and usually has.
You looked at the line just now, do not pretend you did not.
I find these rooms perfectly easy to stand in, Mr Darcy.
Prove, then, that the Meryton rooms do not frighten you.

beats.text: Prove, then, that the Meryton rooms do not frighten you.

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He does not look at the floor, nor at the forming set.
beats.line: "They do not. I remain, as you see, entirely unmoved."

beats.prompt: Captain Carter holds out his hand.

options.text: Take Captain Carter's hand
Thank Captain Carter, and stay where you are
Look at Mr Darcy, and say nothing

beats.text: Look at Mr Darcy, and say nothing

beats.speaker: Mr Darcy
beats.direction: He turns to Captain Carter, unhurried. He extends his hand to Arabella Frost.
beats.line: "The lady is engaged to me for this set, Carter."

beats.text: He leads you down the whole length of the set without a word, every figure correct, and the room turns to watch Mr Darcy dance.
The last figure ends. He bows, and does not let go of your hand quite at once.

beats.title: He Claimed the Set
beats.text: He did not ask. He told Captain Carter you were engaged to him and led you out before you could say otherwise. Charlotte will have to pay. You are not sure yet what it cost him.

beats.identity: Sharpest Wit in the Room  ·  Small Fortune, Large Spirit

moved.why: Arabella Frost answered Darcy's condescension with a cooler line at every turn — catching him looking, drawing an involuntary laugh, naming his audience — and the cumulative effect was that he claimed the set unprompted, meaning her wit did not merely deflect but compelled, proving the theme at its fullest.
